problem.title: Why most QR menus need reprinting
problem.body: Free QR menu tools pack your whole menu inside the QR image itself. It is a neat trick — no hosting, nothing to expire — but it means the code is the menu. Change one price and you get a different code, so every table tent, counter sticker and delivery bag has to be redone. It also caps you at roughly 2,900 characters, about 60–100 dishes.
problem.resolution: Setu QR Menu turns that around. The code points to a permanent link, and the menu behind it is yours to change whenever you like.

faq.question: What happens to my QR code when I change the menu?
faq.answer: Nothing — that is the whole point. The code carries a short permanent link, not the menu, so editing prices, adding dishes or switching to a different menu leaves it untouched. Print once and never reprint.

faq.question: How is this different from the free QR menu generator?
faq.answer: The free tool stores your entire menu inside the QR image, so a new code is produced every time you edit, and the menu is capped at roughly 2,900 characters. Here the menu is stored online, so the code stays fixed, there is no size limit, and you get photos, variations, sold-out toggles, multiple menus and scan analytics.

faq.question: Can I move my menu over from the free tool?
faq.answer: Yes. Paste the menu link from the free tool and every dish comes across, along with your tagline, phone number, address and brand colour. You can also import an Excel or CSV sheet.

faq.question: Do my customers need an app?
faq.answer: No. Any phone camera opens the menu in the browser. The page is deliberately light so it loads fast on a weak connection.

faq.question: Can I change my menu link later?
faq.answer: No, and that is deliberate. The link is what every printed QR code points to, so allowing it to change would silently break signage you have already paid to print. Everything else — your name, logo, colour, currency, dishes — can be changed freely.

faq.question: What happens if I stop paying?
faq.answer: Your menu stops being served and your QR codes show a friendly message instead. Your data is kept, so resubscribing brings the same menu back on the same link.
